question: Honey should not be introduced in any form to infants below 12 months of age because it may contain Clostridium botulinum spores that cause infant botulism.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Honey — including 'natural' or 'organic' honey — is absolutely contraindicated below 12 months because Clostridium botulinum spores can germinate in the infant gut, producing botulinum toxin that causes life-threatening flaccid paralysis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Honey is contraindicated before 12 months due to the risk of infant botulism — Clostridium botulinum spores present in honey can germinate in the immature infant gut, producing the botulinum toxin and causing floppy baby syndrome with respiratory paralysis.
